title: Flag states and registries
description: Where the world's tonnage is registered. This is the legal layer, and it is deliberately decoupled from the economic one: three small states hold roughly half the world's carrying capacity and almost none of its shipowners.

records.name: Liberia
records.note: Largest register in the world by capacity. Eternity C, Magic Seas and Tutor were all Liberian-flagged when they were sunk.

records.name: Panama
records.note: Capacity contracted slightly year on year.

records.name: Bahamas
records.note: Flag of the Galaxy Leader. Capacity contracted year on year.

records.name: Malta
records.note: Flag of the Hellas Aphrodite. Largest register in the European Union.

records.name: Greece
records.note: Flag of the Sounion. Greece is a top-three shipowning nation whose owners mostly register elsewhere — the gap between the ownership and registry tables is the entire point of this dataset.

records.name: United States
records.note: Flag of the Maersk Yorktown. US flag brings US Navy escort — and the Yorktown was fired on anyway.
Most valuable bulker fleet (USD 68.4bn) and container fleet (USD 63.5bn); largest tanker fleet by count at 1,764 vessels, worth USD 47.9bn.
Tanker fleet worth USD 71.3bn, USD 23.3bn more than China's despite fewer hulls. Second-largest LNG fleet: 143 vessels, USD 32.4bn.
Most expensive RoRo fleet at USD 2.6bn across only 40 vessels.
Second-largest owner of vehicle carriers, USD 10.8bn.
Re-entered the top ten on container values and continued MSC investment. A landlocked country in the top ten — ownership is a legal address, not a coastline.

shipowning_nations.gaps: Ranks 2, 5, 6, 7 and 10 were not captured in the source excerpt. Fill from the UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport before using this table.
